answer: Each operator may occupy only one vertex in a public control graph, and every grading seat must publish a signed edge back to that unique node. Opening a second seat from the same operator splits the node and forfeits the bonded stake on every connected edge. A relic account with no current edge is treated as abandoned and carries zero weight. The graph is published in successive shale layers, so later peers can audit earlier admissions and slash any path that collapses to one controller.
